title: Barnard's Loop and the Magellanic Clouds
caption: Barnard's Loop and the Magellanic Clouds over the Atacama Desert, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The plane of the Milky Way arches over the Atacama Desert in northern Chile in this wide panorama by Petr Horálek. Above the band, a half-ring of pink light curves through the sky, and toward the upper right float two pale, diffuse clouds.

The pink arc is Barnard's Loop, a huge, faint shell of glowing gas. It is hard to pick out by eye, but this deep exposure collects enough light to bring it out. Pink and red glows in astronomy photographs usually come from hydrogen gas being energised by nearby stars.

The two pale clouds are the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds, neighbouring galaxies of the Milky Way. Together with the arch of our galaxy and the loop of gas, they make this panorama a gathering of sights that only show up well in long exposures from very dark places.

understand.summary: This is a deep-exposure panoramic landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera in the Atacama Desert. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: Barnard's Loop is very hard to see with the eye alone, but a deep camera exposure gathers enough of its faint light to show the pink arc.

explore: ESO describes this as a deep exposure, which is what lets faint features such as Barnard's Loop show up at all.
alt: The Milky Way arching over a desert, with a faint pink half-ring above it and two pale cloud-like galaxies toward the upper right.
